signals.ai_share_evidence: No AI-generation markers: 2022 repo (pre-agent tooling), commits are manual web-UI edits ('Add files via upload', 'Update app.py'); README is human blog-teaser prose tied to a published Towards AI article.

evidence.excerpt: Metadata: Python, 9 stars, 5 forks, 5 commits by 1 contributor over 2 distinct days (created 2022-10-15, pushed 2022-10-17), no CI, no tests, deps declared, runnable setup not documented.
2022-10-15 'Initial commit', 'Add files via upload', 'Update README.md'; 2022-10-17 'Update README.md', 'Update app.py' — a two-day drop with no later maintenance.
Root entries: README.md, app.py (4143 bytes), cover.png, requirements.txt — a single-script repo with no install or usage docs.

'Scan LinkedIn posts to analyze Emotions, Sentiments, and Trends using AI ... with just a few lines of Python code' ... 'Read the full article here!' (towardsai.net link); no setup or usage instructions in the README itself.

counter_evidence.excerpt: app.py is a real 4.1KB code artifact plus requirements.txt — the promised analysis code exists in the repo, not just in the article.
The repo is explicitly a companion to a published tutorial article ('Read the full article here!'), so the how-to content deliberately lives in the article rather than the README.
'Update app.py' two days after upload shows a follow-up code fix rather than a pure fire-and-forget dump.

strongest_counter_evidence: The deliverable (app.py + requirements.txt) actually exists and matches the article-companion purpose.
Blog-companion repos are simple content by design; under the fairness rules tutorials and simple content are not slop.
A code follow-up edit exists after the initial upload.
counter_evidence_review.review_notes: The heavy template similarity is with the owner's other article-companion repos, which is normal for a tutorial series. The main genuine weakness is that the README makes capability claims (emotions/sentiments/trends analysis) that can only be partially verified from the listing since neither README nor snapshot shows app.py content or setup steps.

notes: Two-day blog-companion repo for a Towards AI article: teaser prose, cover image, and a link out, with a real 4.1KB app.py and requirements.txt but no setup instructions in the README. README structure is near-identical to sibling article repos customer-center-analytics-nlp (and similar to zero-shot-image-classifier), indicating a reused personal article-repo template. Simple tutorial content, not slop, but the specific analysis claims are only structurally corroborated.
